handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, built, or decided in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

known_major_misses_already_identified: STRIP TOPSOIL ROW INCL HAUL OFF: estimate $22,300 vs actual $178,000 (-$155,700). Gemini extracted strip_haul_off_required=false (wrong) AND ROW_SF is understated (Gemini computed 210,395 SF from road_LF × ROW_width; corrected actual is 304,841 SF). Combined these make stripping the single largest miss.

SIGNS & STRIPING: estimate $22,000 vs actual $103,500 (-$81,500). Solara's striping is 5-7× any portfolio analog. Meyer Road is a collector with crosswalks, special signage. CROSSWALK RAPID FLASHING BEACON SYSTEM SIGNS (2 EA × $16,000 = $32,000) also not included.
12" WATER MAIN PVC: estimate $0 vs actual $86,876 (592 LF × $146.75). large_diameter_water_main_present flag apparently not triggered, or no price in KP for 12" main.

EXC TO EMBANK: estimate $50,000 (export_needed) vs actual $127,000 (INCL BORROW & STOCKPILE PH5 — meaning import was needed, not export). Earthwork table showed net cut but job still needed import material for PH5 stockpile.
SWALES: estimate $30,000 vs actual $88,250 (-$58,250). Massively underestimated; Solara's swales are 2-4× any portfolio analog.

ROW_SF Gemini extraction error: Gemini computed 210,395 SF (road_LF 3,507 × ROW_width 60) vs corrected 304,841 SF. ~30% undercount propagated through all ROW_SF-driven scaling formulas (stripping CY, sidewalk SF, sewer/water main LF, curb LF, etc.).
15" SEWER MAIN: entirely missed (312 LF × $98.70 = $30,794). No rule for large-diameter sewer.
60" DROP MANHOLE: entirely missed ($13,500). No rule for drop manholes.
4" BASE ROCK TEMP TURN AROUND: entirely missed (5,520 SY × $9 = $49,680). Phase 2 staging item.
3/6" PAVING MEYER: estimate had a small 3/6" item ($22,755); actual Meyer Road paving alone is $74,415 (1,353 SY × $55). Different scale and spec.
LOT PREP overestimated: estimate $170,000 vs actual STRIP LOTS $61,100 + LOT EXC TO EMBANK $55,500 = $116,600 (-$53,400 over). Settlement Mountain scaling was too aggressive for Solara's lot scope.
diagnostic_themes_to_investigate: ROW_SF extraction failure: Gemini can never compute the correct ROW_SF for jobs like Solara where the ROW polygon includes Meyer Road frontage. Need a different approach — either hand-enter ROW_SF as a CLI override, or add a Gemini prompt instruction to read ROW_SF directly from the qty sheet rather than computing it.
strip_haul_off_required extraction failure: The actual proposal says INCL HAUL OFF but Gemini returned false. Was there a plan note? Did the prompt miss the signal?

Items unique to Solara's scale/type that have no portfolio analog: 15" sewer main, 60" drop manhole, crosswalk beacon systems, temp turn-around, Meyer Road widening paving at $55/SY. These cannot be predicted by any scaling formula — they need separate flags or special-case rules.

Solara is genuinely out-of-distribution: at 304,841 SF ROW and 44 lots, it is 3-4× larger than most portfolio jobs. The only comparable analog is Settlement Mountain (312,291 SF) which is also a Phase 2 / large-scope job. Two data points do not make a reliable regression.
